title: The Lighter Brief
overview: A fairly gentle Sunday: the Panthers grabbed a last-second win to stay atop their division, Akon and Eminem's 'Smack That' went Diamond, and Ludacris finally has a new Walk of Fame date. In Jamaica, the governing JLP held its annual conference amid a debate over hurricane relief, and in Charlotte a local restaurant handed out Thanksgiving turkey money.

stories.headline: I-77 North in Huntersville Reopened After Rollover Crash
stories.summary: A rollover crash near Exit 23 (Gilead Road) closed all northbound lanes of I-77 around noon Sunday. One person was taken to the hospital with serious injuries. The lanes reopened around 2:20 p.m.
key_facts: Location: I-77 North near Exit 23, Gilead Road
Lanes reopened around 2:20 p.m.
Cause not yet known
stories.why: If you drive I-77 through Huntersville, traffic is moving again.

stories.headline: Jamaica's League Leaders Tru-Juice Go for Five Straight Wins
stories.summary: Tru-Juice FC, top of the Jamaica Premier League, faced third-place Racing United on Sunday at Ferdie Neita Park while chasing a fifth straight win. Tyrone Mullings leads the league with eight goals and was facing his old club. Several other matches were also on Sunday's schedule.
key_facts: Tru-Juice have conceded just two goals in a five-game unbeaten run
Mullings and Daniel Roberts have scored 12 of the team's 18 goals
Arnett Gardens' Giovanni Taylor has seven goals
stories.why: A top-of-the-table matchup between two of the league's highest-scoring teams.

links.title: Tru-Juice seek fifth straight win against Racing United

stories.headline: Jamaica's PM Pushes Back on Hurricane Relief Criticism
stories.summary: At the JLP's 83rd annual conference, Prime Minister Andrew Holness urged supporters to push back against what he called lies about how Hurricane Melissa relief has been handed out. He also said he himself is not satisfied with how fast aid has reached people. The government has been in a public back-and-forth with dancehall artist Beenie Man, who has questioned where donations went and released a song called 'Weh di money deh.'
key_facts: The conference was a delegates-only event in Montego Bay
Holness floated a database where people could look up who received aid
Justice Minister Delroy Chuck said last week the government had not explained relief allocation well enough
stories.why: How hurricane relief reaches people is a live public question in Jamaica, and both sides are pressing for clearer answers.

links.title: Holness urges labourites to push back against ‘lies and misinformation’

stories.headline: Panthers Beat the Saints on a Last-Second Field Goal
stories.summary: Ryan Fitzgerald hit a 54-yard field goal as time ran out to give the Carolina Panthers a 20-17 win in New Orleans. Chuba Hubbard was the star, with 172 total yards and two rushing touchdowns. The win keeps Carolina in first place in the NFC South, even though the team committed 17 penalties.
key_facts: Final score: Panthers 20, Saints 17
Hubbard: 92 rushing yards, 80 receiving yards, 2 TDs
Panthers are now 4-5; Saints are 3-6
Panthers host Baltimore next Sunday
stories.why: A walk-off kick for first place is a fun way to end a Sunday if you're a Carolina fan.

stories.headline: About 6,000 Delegates Gather for JLP Conference
stories.summary: Members of the Jamaica Labour Party came to the Montego Bay Convention Centre for the party's 83rd annual conference. This year it was a scaled-back business meeting for delegates only.
key_facts: About 6,000 delegates attended
Held at the Montego Bay Convention Centre, St James
83rd annual conference
stories.why: This was the setting for the party's big announcements this weekend.

stories.headline: JLP Creates $15 Million Fund for Hurricane-Hit Party Workers
stories.summary: Holness announced that the Jamaica Labour Party will set up a $15 million fund to help party workers who are still recovering from Hurricane Melissa. The money will be divided by constituency, and people can be recommended to the party secretariat.
key_facts: $15 million fund from the party treasury
Split up by constituency
Available by the second week of January
stories.why: It's extra recovery help for people still rebuilding after the hurricane.

stories.headline: Akon and Eminem's 'Smack That' Goes Diamond
stories.summary: The RIAA has certified Akon's 2006 hit 'Smack That,' featuring Eminem, as Diamond, which means 10 million U.S. units. In the same update, Akon's 'I Wanna Love You' and 'Don't Matter' reached six-times Platinum. When it first came out, the song made a record jump on the Billboard Hot 100.
key_facts: Diamond award dated November 13, 2026
Diamond = 10 million U.S. units; 150 streams count as one download
In 2006 it jumped from No. 95 to No. 7 on the Hot 100, a record at the time
All three songs are from Akon's 2006 album Konvicted
disputed: Confirmed: the certification appears in the RIAA's official records.
stories.why: A nice reminder that mid-2000s hits are still being played a lot, 20 years later.

links.title: Akon’s “Smack That” With Eminem Earns Diamond Certification

stories.headline: Ludacris and Organized Noize Get a New Walk of Fame Date
stories.summary: The Black Music & Entertainment Walk of Fame ceremony in Atlanta was postponed in June because FIFA-related fencing blocked the site. It now has a new date. Ludacris, Organized Noize, Davido and others will be inducted on February 11, 2027, during Black History Month.
key_facts: New ceremony date: February 11, 2027
Also honored: Davido, Bishop Paul S. Morton, Jack the Rapper and former Atlanta Mayor Maynard H. Jackson
Signia by Hilton Atlanta is the host hotel
Organized Noize produced hits like TLC's 'Waterfalls' and Outkast's 'So Fresh, So Clean'
disputed: Confirmed by an organizers' announcement dated November 13.
stories.why: Atlanta music legends get their delayed moment, and it lands during Black History Month.
